director.chapterArc: Cold arithmetic and forced necessity open the chapter; routine becomes heavy, rhythmic exertion; the near-fall briefly breaks into aftershock and dry humor; the noon examination exposes worsening stakes through clinical observation and eroding memory; the rain descent accelerates through practical urgency; the camp scene contracts into stillness as Jab discovers a power that recognizes Tonk’s illness but cannot help it. End on duty, not despair.
director.restraintNote: Keep Original Calder warm, grounded, and observant. Jab’s panic stays inside counting, procedure, and bodily fatigue; Tonk remains thin and natural, never caricatured. Treat the supernatural response as a quiet physical fact. No yell or hatred is earned, and grief must never bloom into sentimentality.

cues.delivery: A functional reassurance designed to steady Tonk; warmth is present but compressed by fatigue.
cues.reason: Jab establishes protective calm without promising more than he can control.

cues.delivery: Let “Liar” land with fever-dulled but exact childish recognition; keep the touch more important than the joke.
cues.from: "You didn't." Tonk's eyes were shut. His hand came up and patted around until it found Jab's jaw, and stayed there. "Liar."
cues.through: "You didn't." Tonk's eyes were shut. His hand came up and patted around until it found Jab's jaw, and stayed there. "Liar."
cues.reason: Tonk’s sharp clarity briefly relieves the opening tension.

cues.delivery: Dry, exhausted surprise: Tonk’s logic slips past Jab’s defenses and produces a laugh before he can stop it.
cues.from: "Asleep people talk," Tonk said, with his eyes shut and his mouth doing something that was very nearly a grin, and Jab, who had slept perhaps four hours in three days, found that he had laughed.
cues.through: "Asleep people talk," Tonk said, with his eyes shut and his mouth doing something that was very nearly a grin, and Jab, who had slept perhaps four hours in three days, found that he had laughed.
cues.reason: The first genuine release of pressure is small and involuntary.

cues.delivery: Answer as though preserving Tonk’s imagined return costs Jab something; do not expose the full wound.
cues.reason: The repeated assent carries knowledge that Tonk cannot consistently hold.

cues.delivery: The apologies come fast from immediate protective terror, but remain intelligible and physically contained.
cues.from: "Sorry," he said. "Sorry. It's all right. I'm sorry."
cues.through: "Sorry," he said. "Sorry. It's all right. I'm sorry."
cues.reason: Jab has just nearly lost control of Tonk’s weight at the drop.

cues.delivery: Childlike judicial generosity, entirely sincere; let the brevity make it funny.
cues.from: Tonk was silent for a moment. Then, generously: "You can have one more."
cues.through: Tonk was silent for a moment. Then, generously: "You can have one more."
cues.reason: Tonk converts the near-disaster into a rule he understands.

cues.delivery: Carry the fine bodily aftershock beneath the laugh, then settle into the rule with deliberate self-command.
cues.from: Jab put his forehead against the rock and laughed, and it came out shaky. His arms had begun the fine shudder they did afterward. He stayed where he was until it stopped, because this was the tenth time in nine days that something like that had happened, and he had made himself a rule about it after the second: never take the next step angry. The next step was the one that mattered. The one behind him was finished.
cues.through: Jab put his forehead against the rock and laughed, and it came out shaky. His arms had begun the fine shudder they did afterward. He stayed where he was until it stopped, because this was the tenth time in nine days that something like that had happened, and he had made himself a rule about it after the second: never take the next step angry. The next step was the one that mattered. The one behind him was finished.
cues.reason: The danger has passed, but Jab must master the fear before moving.

cues.delivery: Play the jay description as practical nonsense offered for Tonk’s benefit, never as a comic routine.
cues.from: "Everything. He steals from squirrels. He watches where a squirrel puts his nuts, and then he waits until the squirrel goes away, and then he takes them, and then he tells all the other jays about it very loudly, because he can't help it."
cues.through: "Everything. He steals from squirrels. He watches where a squirrel puts his nuts, and then he waits until the squirrel goes away, and then he takes them, and then he tells all the other jays about it very loudly, because he can't help it."
cues.reason: Jab uses play to keep Tonk conscious and connected.

cues.delivery: Hold the lost family evening as an inventory that is quietly shrinking; no nostalgic glow or lament.
cues.from: There was no one about a boat. There had never been one about a boat. There had been an evening in the smoke house in the summer when their father had been in a certain mood and had made up eleven verses about a boat that could not decide where to go, and everybody had contributed a verse, and their mother's verse had been the funniest and had involved the boat's opinion of a particular cousin, and Tonk had been three and had laughed so hard he had fallen off the bench. Nobody had written it down. Nobody wrote anything down.
cues.through: Jab could remember four of the eleven verses. He had been able to remember six in the first week.
cues.reason: The forgotten verses make memory itself another diminishing supply.

cues.delivery: Accept Tonk’s corrections with gentle deadpan; the humor protects the memory they still share.
cues.from: "I'm not," Jab agreed, and sang the four, and Tonk corrected him twice on words he was fairly sure he had right, and Jab let him have both.
cues.through: "I'm not," Jab agreed, and sang the four, and Tonk corrected him twice on words he was fairly sure he had right, and Jab let him have both.
cues.reason: Their teasing briefly restores ordinary family rhythm.

cues.delivery: Keep the first answer mildly indignant, then make the later appeal smaller and more vulnerable without whining.
cues.from: "He's under," Tonk said, from inside, offended on the fish's behalf, and then, a hundred steps later, smaller: "Jab. It's loud."
cues.through: "He's under," Tonk said, from inside, offended on the fish's behalf, and then, a hundred steps later, smaller: "Jab. It's loud."
cues.reason: The enclosing hide and violent rain begin to overwhelm Tonk.

cues.delivery: Explain the sound plainly, lending Tonk calm rather than denying what he hears.
cues.from: "That's just the rain on the hide. It's right by your ear, that's all. It's not as loud out here."
cues.through: "That's just the rain on the hide. It's right by your ear, that's all. It's not as loud out here."
cues.reason: Jab manages fear through concrete information.

cues.delivery: Land the correction—he is not asleep—with clipped, diagnostic dread; make “Quiet” the dangerous fact.
cues.from: Tonk had gone quiet somewhere in the last mile. Not asleep. Quiet.
cues.through: Tonk had gone quiet somewhere in the last mile. Not asleep. Quiet.
cues.reason: Tonk’s silence signals the fever’s worsening turn.

cues.delivery: A minute inward disturbance, observed before it is understood; avoid any mystical flourish.
cues.from: And something under his own breastbone turned over.
cues.through: And something under his own breastbone turned over.
cues.reason: Jab first detects the unexplained response beneath his breastbone.

cues.delivery: Recognize the old metal through exact bodily evidence. Keep the compass comparison investigative, uncanny, and matter-of-fact.
cues.from: It was not his heart. It was under the place his heart was. It was where the metal had gone in, four years ago, when he was thirteen and standing in the river with his whole family on the bar behind him.
cues.through: The rain came down. The fire took a piece of wet fir and spat at him. Under his palm his brother's chest went up, and down, and up, too fast, and something in his own chest went with it — not in time with it, that was the thing, not in time with his own pulse either, but leaning toward it, the way a compass needle leans.
cues.reason: The sensation resolves into a real but unknown action of his power.

cues.delivery: State the uselessness flatly, as a verdict Jab cannot appeal; resist emphasis beyond the sentence’s logic.
cues.from: None of that was any use at all against what was in his brother's leg.
cues.through: None of that was any use at all against what was in his brother's leg.
cues.reason: His proven competence is revealed as irrelevant to Tonk’s illness.

cues.delivery: An inward command spoken barely aloud, using steadiness as something Jab must manufacture.
cues.from: "All right," he said out loud, to nobody, in a voice that sounded almost steady. "All right."
cues.through: "All right," he said out loud, to nobody, in a voice that sounded almost steady. "All right."
cues.reason: He suppresses helplessness and returns himself to action.

cues.delivery: Close in practical devotion: no promise of rescue, only the firm acceptance that Tonk will not face the hour alone.
cues.from: Then he put more wood on the fire, and reset his hand where it had been, and made himself stay awake for the hour that the fever would take to turn, because whatever else was true, that hour was coming and somebody had to be in it with him.
cues.through: Then he put more wood on the fire, and reset his hand where it had been, and made himself stay awake for the hour that the fever would take to turn, because whatever else was true, that hour was coming and somebody had to be in it with him.
cues.reason: Duty becomes the chapter’s restrained answer to helplessness.
